answer: When an AI agent submits a task, it must attach a cryptographic proof of work derived from a stochastic vertex graph that only its hardware can traverse within a bounded time. The ledger records the graph’s ripple pattern; any later submission that mirrors the pattern is automatically rejected, forcing a Sybil node to recompute a fresh graph for each fake identity. The cost scales linearly with the number of identities, turning a gale of cheap clones into an infeasible computational storm.
